what: Continuous Exposures via shift() and scale_tx()
title: Modified Treatment Policies & DR-Learner CATE
text: Asking “every patient received dose = 0 vs. dose = 10?” often forces impossible extrapolations continuous exposures. Modified Treatment Policies solve shifting person’s observed exposure realistically (e.g., +1 unit 90% current dose). Use shift(delta) additive policies d(,w)=+δd(, w) = + \delta scale_tx(factor) multiplicative policies d(,w)=⋅factord(, w) = \cdot \text{factor}. Internally, tidytmle estimates treatment density ratio nonparametrically using stacked cross-validated classification workflows without parametric normality assumptions:
code: library(tidytmle)  df_cont <- sim_causal_cohort(   n = 350,   outcome_type = "continuous",   treatment_type = "continuous",   seed = 202 ) truth_cont <- attr(df_cont, "truth")  # Additive shift (+1 unit) fit_shift <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   estimand   = shift(1.0) ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 4L) |>   fit(data = df_cont)  # Multiplicative policy (90% of current dose) fit_scale <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   estimand   = scale_tx(0.9) ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 4L) |>   fit(data = df_cont)  summary(fit_shift) #>  #> ── Plain-English TMLE Summary ── #>  #> Sample: 350 rows (350 observed outcomes) | 4-fold CV-TMLE #>  #> ── 1. What the Causal Estimates Mean  #> ℹ shift(1): Expected outcome under Modified Treatment Policy is 4.8277 (95% CI [4.4089, 5.2465], p = < 0.0001). #>  #> ── 2. What the Targeting Step Did  #> Fluctuating along the Clever Covariate shifted the initial ML plug-in #> estimate by +0.2184 (epsilon = 0.0653) to remove residual confounding #> bias. #>  #> ── 3. Statistical Health Check & Next Steps  #> ✔ Convergence: EIF estimating equation solved (mean EIF = -9.51e-14). #> ✔ Positivity: 0.0% clipped at g_bounds [0.000, 21.918] (ESS: treated = 116.3, control = 350). #> ! High leverage: Top observation accounts for 37.2% of EIF variance. Inspect `augment(fit)` sorted by .eif_leverage. dplyr::bind_rows(tidy(fit_shift), tidy(fit_scale)) |>   dplyr::mutate(true_value = c(truth_cont$true_shift_1, truth_cont$true_scale_09)) #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   estimand      term    estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low #>   <chr>         <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 shift(1)      shift(…     4.83     0.214      22.6 5.10e-113     4.41 #> 2 scale_tx(0.9) scale_…     3.67     0.125      29.3 7.78e-189     3.43 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: conf.high <dbl>, true_value <dbl>  autoplot(fit_shift, type = "overlap")

text: Applied papers repeatedly highlight three pitfalls break naive TMLE implementations practice. tidytmle enables defenses three automatically: Cross-Validated TMLE (cv_tmle = TRUE, Zheng & van der Laan, 2011): Flexible tree/boosting learners routinely violate classical Donsker class smoothness assumptions, causing -sample TMLE standard errors anti-conservative (CIs narrow). --fold cross-fitting via rsample restores valid asymptotic normality without restricting learner library. Bounded Canonical Logistic Fluctuation (fluctuation = "logistic", Gruber & van der Laan, 2010): Linear fluctuations unbounded outcomes can overshoot impossible values confounding. Scaling continuous YY [0,1][0, 1], running canonical logistic submodel, transforming back guarantees counterfactual predictions remain inside observed outcome range. Adaptive Positivity Truncation (g_bounds = "adaptive", Petersen et al., 2012): Rather clipping propensities rigid 0.025 regardless sample size, tidytmle defaults nn-aware 5/(neffln⁡neff)5 / (\sqrt{n_{\text{eff}}} \ln n_{\text{eff}}) rule (bounded [0.01, 0.15]), reports pct_truncated Kish effective sample sizes (ess_treated, ess_control), lets run instant positivity sensitivity sweep via retarget() autoplot(fit, type = "sensitivity").

title: Extract 1-Row Causal Health Check from a TMLE Fit — glance.tmle_fit
text: mean_eif: sample average Efficient Influence Function \(\frac{1}{n}\sum D_i^*\). healthy TMLE solves EIF score equation, abs(mean_eif) must near zero (< 1e-4). epsilon: magnitude targeting fluctuation step. Values close 0 mean initial ML outcome fit already little residual confounding bias; larger magnitudes show strongly TMLE adjusted initial predictions remove bias. plugin_vs_tmle_shift: Difference final targeted TMLE ATE untargeted G-computation plug-ATE. Quantifies exact causal bias correction performed targeting step. pct_truncated & ess_treated/ess_control: Share propensity scores clipped [g_bound_low, g_bound_high] Kish's effective sample size inverse-propensity weighting. High truncation (> 5%) tiny ESS signals near-positivity violations (Petersen et al., 2012). max_eif_leverage: Largest single observation's share total EIF variance. Values > 0.10 flag influential observation dominating standard error.

title: Configure TMLE Targeting, Positivity Bounds, and Memory Options — set_targeting
text: Three built-statistical guardrails govern targeting step: CV-TMLE (cv_tmle = TRUE): Uses --fold nuisance predictions standard errors remain valid even using non-Donsker machine learning learners random forests boosted trees (Zheng & van der Laan, 2011). Adaptive Positivity Truncation (g_bounds = "adaptive"): Prevents handful near-0 near-1 propensity scores inflating inverse weights EIF variance, following sample-size-aware \(5 / (\sqrt{n}\ln n)\) diagnostic rule (Petersen et al., 2012; Gruber & van der Laan, 2010). Bounded Logistic Fluctuation (fluctuation = "logistic"): Scales continuous outcomes [0, 1] performs canonical logistic fluctuation targeted counterfactual predictions stay strictly inside observed support even extreme confounding (Gruber & van der Laan, 2010).

title: Modified Treatment Policy Constructors for Continuous Exposures — shift
text: Unlike static binary interventions ("treat everyone vs. treat one"), continuous exposures often violate positivity try force every individual exact dose. Modified Treatment Policies avoid extrapolation shifting person's observed exposure realistically: shift(delta) defines additive shift \(d(, w) = + \delta\) (e.g., increasing daily exercise +15 minutes reducing dose -1 unit). scale_tx(factor) defines multiplicative policy \(d(, w) = \cdot \text{factor}\) (e.g., reducing exposure 10%). tidytmle estimates post-intervention density ratio \(g_d(\mid w) / g(\mid w)\) nonparametrically via stacked cross-validated classification without parametric normality assumptions.
